mainTopic: The sources and order of the שופר blasts on ראש השנה, and רבי אבהו's sets of שברים and תרועה
overview: This amud builds the order of the שופר blasts on ראש השנה from the פסוקים. One ברייתא uses the extra words 'in the seventh month' and a גזירה שוה on 'seventh' to give three sets of תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה, nine blasts in all. The גמרא explains that this ברייתא's היקש was only a backup to its גזירה שוה. A second ברייתא learns the plain blasts before and after each תרועה from the trumpets in the מדבר, and carries them over to ראש השנה with a גזירה שוה on the word תרועה. That ברייתא counts two תרועות as Torah law and one as from the חכמים, while רבי יונתן counts only one as Torah law. The גמרא then works out where each opinion learns that the שופר is blown by day, the rules of רב מתנא, and that a שופר, not a trumpet, is used. Finally, רבי אבהו's practice in קיסרי of blowing שברים and תרועה is explained as covering the doubt about what the Torah's תרועה sounds like. The amud ends as the גמרא begins רבי יוחנן's comment on stretching one blast to count as two, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An extra phrase teaches that all seventh-month blasts are alike
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the words 'in the seventh month' are not needed in the פסוק. It uses them to teach that all the שופר soundings of the seventh month must be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse did not need to say 'in the seventh month.' So why does it say it? To teach that all the שופר soundings of the seventh month must be like one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes a derivation it started earlier. A phrase in the פסוק is not needed, so it must be there to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the יובל year already says 'on יום הכפורים,' so we already know the month. That makes 'in the seventh month' extra. The extra words teach that the blasts of ראש השנה and of the יובל on יום כיפור, both in תשרי, follow the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches / the verse says (used to bring a source or to ask why a phrase is there)
This one like that one; the same as each other

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole idea that the שופר rules of ראש השנה and of the יובל are one shared system.

phrases.english: Since there is no need for the verse to say 'in the seventh month,'
phrases.notes: The פסוק already says 'on יום הכפורים,' so we already know which month it is (ויקרא 25:9).

phrases.english: what does the verse come to teach by saying 'in the seventh month'?
That all the shofar soundings of the seventh month should be
like one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation the ברייתא began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the שופר soundings of the seventh month must follow the same pattern.

steps.title: Asking for the source of three sets of three blasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that there are three sets, each made of three blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that there are three sets of three blasts each?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a new question. It is setting up the next move, which is a source from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we know each set is תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה. The new question is about how many sets there must be: why three?

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Three sets of three blasts each

phrases.english: And from where do we know three sets of three blasts each?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'all blasts are alike' to 'how many sets are there.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for having three sets of blasts.

steps.title: Three verses mention תרועה, so there are three sets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings three פסוקים that each say תרועה, which gives three sets of blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'You shall sound the שופר, a תרועה'; 'a day of rest, a remembrance of תרועה'; 'it shall be a day of תרועה for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by quoting three פסוקים that each use the word תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mention of תרועה counts as one set. Earlier in the ברייתא, every תרועה was shown to have a plain blast before it and after it. So three mentions give three sets of תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall sound the שופר (said about the יובל)

steps.confusionAlert: These three פסוקים are not all about the same day. Two are about ראש השנה (ויקרא 23:24, במדבר 29:1), and one is about the יובל on יום כיפור (ויקרא 25:9). That is exactly why the next step needs a way to share the rules between them.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'You shall sound the shofar, a teruah,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9

phrases.english: 'a day of rest, a remembrance of teruah,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24

phrases.english: 'it shall be a day of teruah for you.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three mentions of תרועה in the פסוקים give three sets of blasts.

steps.title: How can rules from one occasion apply to the other?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know to take what is said about one occasion and apply it to the other, in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know to apply what is said about this one to that one, and what is said about that one to this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a gap in the proof it just gave. It is setting up the next step, which fills that gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three פסוקים are not all about the same day: some are about ראש השנה and one is about the יובל on יום כיפור. To add them up into three sets for each day, we need a way to share their details both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: What belongs to this one, in that one

phrases.english: And from where do we know to apply what is said

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה וְשֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: about this one to that one, and about that one to this one?
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are ראש השנה and the יובל on יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the proof in step 3 mixes פסוקים about two different days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that lets the two occasions share their שופר rules.

steps.title: The word 'seventh' links the two days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'seventh' appears with both occasions, so their rules are shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'seventh' here and 'seventh' there, for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא fills the gap with a גזירה שוה built on the shared word 'seventh.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'seventh' appears in the פסוק about ראש השנה and in the פסוק about the יובל. That shared word links the two, so every detail said about one applies to the other. Now each day gets all three mentions of תרועה, which means three sets on each day.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching built on the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Three mentions of תרועה, together with the 'seventh-seventh' גזירה שוה, give three sets of תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה on both ראש השנה and the יובל.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'seventh,' 'seventh,'
phrases.notes: One 'seventh' is in the פסוק about the יובל, the other in the פסוק about ראש השנה (ויקרא 25:9; 23:24).

phrases.english: for a gezeirah shavah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'seventh' creates a גזירה שוה that shares the rules between the two days.

steps.title: The practical result: nine blasts and the length of each
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up. There are three sets, which make nine blasts. A תקיעה lasts as long as a תרועה, and a תרועה lasts as long as three שברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work? Three sets, which are nine blasts. A תקיעה is as long as a תרועה, and a תרועה is as long as three שברים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by spelling out how the blowing is actually done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three sets of three blasts give nine blasts in all. The ברייתא also gives lengths: a תקיעה equals one תרועה, and a תרועה equals three short שברים.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How does this work in practice?

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה said a תקיעה is as long as three תרועות, and a תרועה is as long as three יבבות. This ברייתא gives different measures, so do not mix them up.
steps.whatToRemember: Nine blasts in total. Per this ברייתא: a תקיעה equals one תרועה, and a תרועה equals three שברים.
steps.whyThisMatters: These measures set how long each blast must be.

phrases.english: How so?
Three sets, which are nine blasts.
The length of a tekiah is like a teruah,
the length of a teruah is like three shevarim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the derivations into the practical order and lengths of the blasts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nine blasts in three sets. A תקיעה equals a תרועה in length, and a תרועה equals three שברים.

steps.title: Why did the תנא switch methods?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the same תנא first used a היקש and then used a גזירה שוה for the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא first brought the rule from a היקש, and now he brings it from a גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the ברייתא we just finished. One teacher seems to use two different methods to prove the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1, the ברייתא linked all the blasts of the seventh month through the extra phrase 'בחודש השביעי', which works as a היקש. Then in step 5 the same תנא used a גזירה שוה on the word 'seventh'. Why would he need both, or switch in the middle?

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the time of the משנה and ברייתא
Learning a rule because two things are placed side by side in a פסוק
Learning a rule because the same word shows up in two places

steps.confusionAlert: A היקש and a גזירה שוה are two different tools. A היקש uses things placed next to each other in a פסוק. A גזירה שוה uses a matching word.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא, מֵעִיקָּרָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בְּהֶיקֵּישָׁא,
phrases.english: This tanna at first brings it from a juxtaposition,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 1, where the extra words 'בחודש השביעי' made all the seventh-month blasts alike.

phrases.english: and now he brings it from a verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא, מֵעִיקָּרָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בְּהֶיקֵּישָׁא, וְהַשְׁתָּא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the ברייתא's method and points out that it seems to change.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the ברייתא proves its rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One תנא should not need two different proofs, or switch methods partway, for one rule.

steps.title: The היקש was only a backup
steps.stepSummary: The תנא means that he would have used the היקש if there were no גזירה שוה. Since there is one, the היקש is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if not for the גזירה שוה, I would have brought it from the היקש. Now that it comes from a גזירה שוה, the היקש is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The תנא is not using two proofs. He is saying which proof he would fall back on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש is a 'plan B'. The real source is the גזירה שוה on 'seventh'. So there is no double proof and no switch in method.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If not for the verbal analogy,
I would have brought it from the juxtaposition.
Now that it comes from a verbal analogy,
the juxtaposition is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִי לָאו גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, הֲוָה מַיְיתִינָא לַהּ בְּהֶיקֵּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the היקש was only a backup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא used two proofs, or changed his method.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה is the real source. The היקש would only be used if there were no גזירה שוה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first ברייתא, the main source is the גזירה שוה on 'seventh'. The היקש is only a backup.

steps.title: A second ברייתא learns from the מדבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that another תנא learns the שופר rules by a גזירה שוה from the trumpets in the מדבר. That ברייתא opens by saying a תקיעה and a תרועה are separate sounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this other תנא brings it with a גזירה שוה from the מדבר, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall sound a תרועה': a תקיעה is its own sound, and a תרועה is its own sound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא with a different source. Its first claim is that a תקיעה and a תרועה are two different sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source here is not the word 'seventh'. It is the trumpet blasts in the מדבר. The ברייתא first has to make sure that 'תקיעה' and 'תרועה' really mean two different sounds.

keyTerms.meaning: The wilderness. Here it means the trumpet blasts the Jews used there

phrases.english: And this tanna brings it
by verbal analogy from the wilderness,
phrases.notes: He means the silver trumpets blown in the מדבר.

phrases.english: as it is taught: “And you shall sound a terua”:
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:5

phrases.english: a tekia is its own sound
and a terua is its own sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה מִמִּדְבָּר, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that uses a different source for the shofar rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תקיעה and a תרועה are two separate sounds.

steps.title: Maybe תקיעה and תרועה are one sound?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the two words might just be two names for the same sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say a תקיעה is its own sound and a תרועה is its own sound? Or maybe a תקיעה and a תרועה are one and the same?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own claim. It raises the other possibility so it can disprove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ותקעתם תרועה' uses both words together. Someone could read it as one sound with two names. The ברייתא needs a proof that they are different.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say…? (opens a test of a claim)
They are one and the same

phrases.english: Do you say a tekia is its own sound
and a terua is its own sound,
or is it only that
a tekia and a terua are one and the same?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר תְּקִיעָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ וּתְרוּעָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim made in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are תקיעה and תרועה two sounds or one?

steps.title: Proof from gathering the people
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to do a תקיעה but not a תרועה when gathering the people. So they must be different sounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says, 'When gathering the people, you shall do a תקיעה and not a תרועה', you must say a תקיעה is its own sound and a תרועה is its own sound.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a פסוק that sets the two sounds against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תקיעה and תרועה were the same sound, the Torah could not say 'do this one but not that one'. So they must be two different sounds.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, so it must be

phrases.english: When it says:
“But when the assembly is gathered together,
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:7

phrases.english: you shall sound a tekia but not a terua,”
you must say: a tekia is its own sound
and a terua is its own sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: וּבְהַקְהִיל אֶת הַקָּהָל תִּתְקְעוּ וְלֹא תָרִיעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah separates them in one פסוק, so they are two different sounds.

steps.title: A plain blast comes before the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'ותקעתם תרועה' that a plain blast comes before each תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know there is a plain blast before it? The פסוק says: 'And you shall sound a תקיעה, a תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks about the order of the sounds. It brings a פסוק to show a plain blast goes before the תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'ותקעתם תרועה' the word for תקיעה comes first and תרועה comes second. That order teaches that a תקיעה is blown before the תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: A straight, plain blast, meaning a תקיעה

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes before it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the תרועה, and the 'straight blast' is a תקיעה.

phrases.english: The verse states: “And you shall sound a terua.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the sounds are known to be separate, the ברייתא moves on to their order.
steps.raayaObject: A תקיעה must come before the תרועה

steps.title: A plain blast comes after the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'תרועה יתקעו' that a plain blast also comes after each תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know there is a plain blast after it? The פסוק says: 'A תרועה, they shall do a תקיעה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the order of the sounds. Here the word תרועה comes first and the word for תקיעה comes after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק the order is flipped, so a תקיעה follows the תרועה. Put this together with step 12 and you get תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה.
steps.whatToRemember: Every תרועה is surrounded by plain blasts: תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes after it?
The verse states: “A terua they shall sound.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches step 12, now for the blast after the תרועה.
steps.raayaObject: A תקיעה must come after the תרועה

steps.title: The extra word 'שנית' teaches the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says that proof is not needed. The extra word 'שנית' teaches that every תרועה has a תקיעה second to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: that is not needed. The פסוק says 'And you shall sound a תרועה a second time'. The word 'second' is not needed, so why does it say 'second'? This is a בנין אב: wherever it says תרועה, a תקיעה should come second to it.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives his own source for the plain blast after the תרועה. He uses a word in the פסוק that seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from the context that this is the second set of blasts, so the word 'שנית' seems unneeded. רבי ישמעאל reads it as a general rule, a בנין אב, that every תרועה has a תקיעה after it. So he does not need the ברייתא's proof from 'תרועה יתקעו'.

keyTerms.meaning: A model case that sets a rule for all similar cases

steps.confusionAlert: 'שניה לה' here means a תקיעה that comes second to the תרועה, right after it. It does not mean a second תרועה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, the son of
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
It is not necessary,
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא's proof from 'תרועה יתקעו' isn't needed.

phrases.english: for it says:
“And you shall sound a terua a second time,”
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:6

phrases.english: since the verse did not need to say “a second time,”
so why does the verse say “a second time”?
This sets up a model rule,
that in every place where “terua” is said,
there should be a tekia second to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for what step 13 proved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the extra word 'שנית', every תרועה must have a תקיעה after it.

steps.title: What about ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The rule so far was learned about the trumpets in the מדבר. The ברייתא asks how we know it also applies to ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only have this for the מדבר. How do we know it for ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap. Everything so far was about the מדבר, but our topic is the שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים quoted are all about the trumpets in the מדבר. To use this rule for the שופר, we need a link between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year, when the shofar is blown

phrases.english: I have this only in the wilderness;
from where do we know it on Rosh HaShana?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּמִּדְבָּר, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the rule from the מדבר to ראש השנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What links the rules of the מדבר to ראש השנה?

steps.title: The word תרועה links them
steps.stepSummary: The word תרועה is used for both the מדבר and ראש השנה. This makes a גזירה שוה, so the rules carry over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'תרועה' and 'תרועה' to make a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word shows up in both places, so the same rules apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both the מדבר and ראש השנה use the word תרועה, the rule of a plain blast around each תרועה moves over to the shofar. This is the 'גזירה שוה from the מדבר' that the גמרא promised in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The same word, תרועה, used in both places
To make a גזירה שוה, a link through a matching word

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא learns the shofar blasts from the trumpets in the מדבר. The link to ראש השנה is a גזירה שוה on the word תרועה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the shofar on ראש השנה follows the pattern תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
“terua,” “terua,” for a verbal analogy.
phrases.notes: One 'תרועה' is in the פסוק about the מדבר, and the other is in the פסוק about ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: תְּרוּעָה תְּרוּעָה לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word תרועה carries the rules of the מדבר over to ראש השנה.

steps.title: Three פסוקים say תרועה for ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists three פסוקים that use the word תרועה for ראש השנה, and says each one gets two תקיעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three תרועות are mentioned for ראש השנה: 'שבתון זכרון תרועה', 'יום תרועה', and 'והעברת שופר תרועה'. Each one has two תקיעות.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the rules of the מדבר carry over to ראש השנה, the ברייתא counts how many times the Torah says תרועה for ראש השנה. It finds three, and gives each one a תקיעה before and after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12-14 taught that every תרועה has a plain blast before it and after it. Step 16 carried that rule over to ראש השנה. So now each of the three תרועות gets two תקיעות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A day of rest, a remembrance of תרועה' (ויקרא 23:24)
'You shall sound the shofar of תרועה' (ויקרא 25:9)

phrases.english: And three teruot are stated about Rosh HaShana:
"A solemn rest, a memorial of terua"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24

phrases.english: "A day of terua"
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:1

phrases.english: "Then you shall sound the shofar of terua"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9

phrases.english: And two tekiot for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the גזירה שוה from Step 16 to apply the before-and-after rule to the three ראש השנה פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three תרועות for ראש השנה, each with a תקיעה before and after.

steps.title: Three תרועות and six תקיעות: two from the Torah, one from the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up: three תרועות and six תקיעות. Two תרועות are from the Torah, and one is from the חכמים, because 'יום תרועה' is used for its own teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we learn: three תרועות and six תקיעות for ראש השנה. Two are Torah law and one is from the חכמים. 'שבתון זכרון תרועה' and 'והעברת שופר תרועה' are Torah law. 'יום תרועה יהיה לכם' comes for its own teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds up the total and then explains that not all three count the same. One of the פסוקים is used up for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יום תרועה' was used in Step 16 to build the גזירה שוה. Since that פסוק is busy teaching something else, its תרועה does not count as a full Torah obligation. The חכמים still made it a requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We find that we have learned': a summing-up phrase
'It comes for its own teaching': the פסוק is used for a different lesson

steps.whatToRemember: The total is three תרועות and six תקיעות. The ברייתא says two of the תרועות are from the Torah and one is from the חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: 'From the חכמים' does not mean the third תרועה is optional. We still blow it. It just isn't counted as a direct Torah obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic number of blasts for ראש השנה that the rest of the sugya builds on.

phrases.english: We find that we have learned:
Three teruot and six tekiot
are stated about Rosh HaShana,
two by the words of the Torah,
and one by the words of the Sages.
"A solemn rest, a memorial of terua" and "Then you shall sound the shofar of terua"
are by the words of the Torah.
"It shall be a day of terua for you"
comes for its own teaching.
phrases.notes: This פסוק is the one used for the גזירה שוה in Step 16, so it's busy teaching that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Totals the count from Step 17 and sorts the תרועות into Torah and rabbinic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three תרועות and six תקיעות. Two תרועות are from the Torah and one is from the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: only one תרועה is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני quotes רבי יונתן: only 'והעברת שופר תרועה' is Torah law. The other two פסוקים are each used for their own teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: one is from the Torah and two are from the חכמים. 'והעברת שופר תרועה' is Torah law. 'שבתון זכרון תרועה' and 'יום תרועה יהיה לכם' come for their own teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion is brought. It flips the ברייתא's split: one תרועה from the Torah, two from the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said only 'יום תרועה' was busy with another lesson. רבי יונתן says 'שבתון זכרון תרועה' is also busy with its own lesson. So only one פסוק is left to count as a Torah obligation.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
One by the words of the Torah,
and two by the words of the Sages.
"Then you shall sound the shofar of terua" is by the words of the Torah.
"A solemn rest, a memorial of terua"
and "It shall be a day of terua for you"
each comes for its own teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 18 about how many of the three תרועות are from the Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one תרועה is from the Torah. Two are from the חכמים.

steps.title: What is the 'own teaching'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lesson the פסוק is being used for, if it does not count as a Torah obligation for a תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it comes for its own teaching' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what that extra lesson actually is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a פסוק is 'busy with its own teaching' only works if we know what it teaches. The גמרא wants that lesson spelled out.

phrases.english: What does "it comes for its own teaching" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to explain the phrase used in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the פסוק teaches instead of adding a Torah-level תרועה.

steps.title: It teaches: blow by day, not at night
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק is needed to teach that the שופר is blown during the day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to teach: by day, and not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק teaches the time for blowing: daytime only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'יום תרועה', a DAY of תרועה. The word 'day' teaches that the מצוה is during the day, not at night. Since the פסוק is used for this, it is not counted as an extra Torah-level תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed': this פסוק is needed for a different lesson

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'יום' in 'יום תרועה' teaches that shofar is blown only by day.

phrases.english: It is needed to teach:
by day and not at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that shofar is blown during the day, not at night.

steps.title: Where does the other opinion learn 'by day, not by night'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the other opinion knows the shofar is blown only by day, since it uses 'יום תרועה' for a different purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion: where does it learn that the shofar is blown by day and not at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion and asks where it gets the rule that the shofar is blown by day. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, רבי יונתן learned 'by day, not at night' from 'יום תרועה'. The other opinion, the ברייתא that learns from the מדבר (steps 9-18), uses that phrase for its גזירה שוה from the מדבר. So it needs a different source for the daytime rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
By day and not at night
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And the other one,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that learns from the מדבר. It already uses 'יום תרועה' for its גזירה שוה, so it can't use it for the daytime rule.

phrases.english: by day and not at night, from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the daytime source from Step 21 back to the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that the shofar is blown by day, according to the opinion that does not use 'יום תרועה' for it.

steps.title: He learns it from 'On the Day of Atonement'
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion learns the daytime rule from the יובל verse 'ביום הכפורים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'On the Day of Atonement.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this opinion learns the daytime rule from the shofar of יובל, which is blown 'ביום הכפורים', meaning on the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ביום' in the יובל verse shows the blowing is by day. That rule is then applied to ראש השנה as well. So 'יום תרועה' stays free for this opinion's גזירה שוה from the מדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (literally, it comes out for him)
On the Day of Atonement (ויקרא 25:9, about יובל)

phrases.english: He derives it
from 'On the Day of Atonement.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9. That verse is about blowing shofar in the יובל year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daytime rule comes from the יובל verse 'ביום הכפורים'.

steps.title: Then learn the plain blasts from the יובל verse too
steps.stepSummary: If this opinion learns from the יובל verse, it should also learn the plain תקיעה before and after each תרועה from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns from 'On the Day of Atonement,' let us also learn from it a plain blast before the תרועה and a plain blast after it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: if you are already learning from the יובל verse, why not learn the plain blasts before and after each תרועה from that same verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same יובל verse says 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו', which seem to hint at plain blasts. Since this opinion already uses that verse for one rule, it should use it for this rule too. Then it would not need to learn the plain blasts from the trumpets in the מדבר.

phrases.english: If he learns from 'On the Day of Atonement,'
let us also learn from it
a plain blast before it
phrases.notes: 'It' means each תרועה.

phrases.english: and a plain blast after it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים״ יָלֵיף, נִגְמוֹר נָמֵי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 23 by pushing it further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The other opinion's use of the יובל verse for the daytime rule only.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the יובל verse is a valid source for one shofar rule, it should also be the source for the plain blasts mentioned in that same verse.

steps.title: Those words do not mean plain blasts to them
steps.stepSummary: The words 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' do not teach plain blasts according to this opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Then you shall make proclamation' and 'You shall make proclamation' do not mean that to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this opinion does not read 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' as hints to plain blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the daytime rule from 'ביום הכפורים' does not force you to take every rule from that verse. The words 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' are needed for other lessons, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall make pass (proclaim) — ויקרא 25:9
You shall make pass (proclaim) — same verse
It does not mean that to them

phrases.english: 'Then you shall make proclamation,' 'you shall make proclamation'
phrases.notes: Both words are in ויקרא 25:9.

phrases.english: do not mean that to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse differently: the words in question are not a hint to plain blasts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the יובל verse is used for one rule, it should also teach the plain blasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: This opinion does not read 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' as plain blasts, so the plain blasts must come from elsewhere.

steps.title: So what do they learn from those words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this opinion does learn from 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do they learn from them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if these words do not teach plain blasts, what do they teach? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the Torah should teach something. Since Step 25 said these words do not teach plain blasts, the גמרא wants to know what lesson they do carry.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they learn from them?

phrases.english: Rather, what do they learn from them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 25 by asking what the words do teach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lessons this opinion learns from 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו'.

steps.title: They follow רב מתנא's two lessons
steps.stepSummary: 'והעברת' teaches that the shofar keeps the shape the animal carried it in; 'תעבירו' teaches that the shofar must be blown, not just carried.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'והעברת' is learned like רב מתנא. For רב מתנא said: 'והעברת' means the way it was carried. 'תעבירו' is there because the Torah said it so you would not think: let us just carry it by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב מתנא: each of the two words teaches its own rule about the shofar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והעברת' is related to carrying, so it teaches that the shofar must be used in the shape the animal carried it on its head. 'תעבירו' is there so no one thinks 'make it pass' means just carrying the shofar around by hand instead of blowing it. With both words used up, they cannot teach the plain blasts.

keyTerms.meaning: The way it was carried (as the animal carried the horn)

phrases.english: 'Veha'avarta' is learned like רב מתנא.
For רב מתנא said:
'Veha'avarta': the way it was carried,
phrases.notes: He means the shofar must keep the shape the animal carried it in: the narrow end stays narrow and the wide end stays wide.

phrases.english: 'Ta'aviru': because the Torah said it
so you would not say: let us carry it by hand.
phrases.notes: 'Make it pass' could be misread as carrying the shofar around the land, so the Torah makes clear it means blowing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words teach רב מתנא's two rules: the shofar is used in its natural shape, and it must be blown, not just carried.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Veha'avarta' and 'ta'aviru' come from the same root, 'make pass'. Here each one teaches a different rule: one about the shape of the shofar, one about actually blowing it.

steps.title: And the other opinion: where does it learn רב מתנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the other opinion, which uses these words for the plain blasts, learns רב מתנא's rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the opinion that does use 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' for the plain blasts. Where does it get רב מתנא's rules? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If those words are used up teaching the plain blasts, they seem unavailable for רב מתנא's lessons. So the other opinion needs a different source for them.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is the opinion that learns the plain blasts from these words. Where does it get רב מתנא's rules?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of Step 27 back to the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רב מתנא's rules for the opinion that uses 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' for the plain blasts.

steps.title: He learns רב מתנא from the unusual wording
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion learns רב מתנא's rules from the fact that the Torah used an unusual word instead of the regular word for blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns רב מתנא's rule from the fact that the verse changed its usual wording.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah chose an unusual word ('make pass' instead of 'blow'), and that change itself teaches רב מתנא's rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the Torah would say 'blow' for a shofar. Choosing 'make pass' is a change, and that change teaches רב מתנא's lessons. So the words can teach the plain blasts and the unusual choice of wording teaches רב מתנא, which means both opinions have a source for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: It changed its wording (used an unusual word)

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree the shofar is blown by day; they only disagree about the source. One learns it from 'יום תרועה', the other from 'ביום הכפורים'. 'והעברת' and 'תעבירו' teach רב מתנא's rules, and for one opinion they also teach the plain blasts, with רב מתנא learned from the unusual wording.

phrases.english: The rule of רב מתנא,
he learns from the fact that the verse changed its wording.
phrases.notes: The Torah could have said 'blow' but said 'make pass' instead, and that change is the hint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 28; step 30 then fills the last gap for this opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב מתנא's rules are learned from the Torah's unusual choice of wording.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each opinion has a complete set of sources: the daytime rule, the plain blasts, and רב מתנא's rules are all accounted for.

steps.title: Blowing, not carrying, is learned from משה
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that uses 'והעברת' for the plain blasts still knows the שופר must make a sound, because it learns 'passing' from משה, where it meant a sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say 'תעבירו' means just carrying the שופר by hand, because this תנא learns the word 'passing' from the same word used by משה. Here it says 'You shall pass a שופר of תרועה', and there it says 'משה commanded, and they passed a voice through the camp.' Just as there it was with a sound, here too it must be with a sound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: if this opinion uses these words for the plain blasts, how does it know the שופר must be blown and not just carried? It answers with a word-link to a פסוק about משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 27, the other opinion used 'תעבירו' to teach that the שופר must be blown. This opinion used that word for something else, so it needs another source. It finds one in a גזירה שוה: the same word 'pass' is used with משה, where it clearly meant passing a sound through the camp.

keyTerms.meaning: by hand (just carrying it, not blowing)
'passing', the shared root in both פסוקים
just as there, so too here (how a word-link carries a rule over)

phrases.english: And as for reading 'You shall pass' as carrying by hand —
you cannot say that,
because he learns 'passing' and 'passing' from משה.
It is written here: 'You shall pass a shofar of teruah,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9

phrases.english: and it is written there:
'And Moshe commanded, and they passed a voice through the camp,'
phrases.notes: שמות 36:6

phrases.english: just as there it was with a sound,
so too here it must be with a sound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills the remaining gap for the opinion in Step 29: where it learns that the שופר must be blown.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source through a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'תעבירו' free to teach it, maybe this opinion would let one just carry the שופר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word-link to משה's announcement in the camp shows that 'passing' means passing a sound.

steps.title: Should we use trumpets like in the wilderness?
steps.stepSummary: If one תנא learns the blowing pattern from the trumpet blasts in the wilderness, maybe ראש השנה should also need trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to this תנא, who learns it from the wilderness: if so, just as there they used trumpets, here too we should use trumpets?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a תנא from earlier who learned the pattern of תקיעה before and after the תרועה from the trumpet blasts in the wilderness. If we copy the pattern from there, why not copy the instrument too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries over the details of the case it comes from. In the wilderness the blasts were on silver trumpets, so the comparison seems to require trumpets on ראש השנה as well. The גמרא now needs a reason the comparison stops short of that.

keyTerms.meaning: the wilderness, where בני ישראל traveled

phrases.english: And according to this תנא
who brings it from the wilderness,
phrases.notes: Earlier, this תנא learned the pattern of a plain blast before and after the תרועה from the trumpet blasts in במדבר 10.

phrases.english: if so, just as there it was trumpets,
so too here it should be trumpets?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different תנא's source and tests how far his comparison reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא who learns the blowing pattern from the trumpets in the wilderness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wilderness case is the model, its instrument (trumpets) should carry over too.

steps.title: The פסוק says שופר for ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים says to blow a שופר on the festival when the moon is covered, which is ראש השנה, so trumpets are ruled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Blow a שופר at the new month, at the covered time, for our festival day.' Which festival has the moon covered on it? That is ראש השנה. And the Torah says 'שופר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק that names the instrument directly. Since ראש השנה is the only festival at the start of the month, when the moon is hidden, the פסוק is about ראש השנה, and it says 'שופר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to the wilderness teaches the pattern of the blasts, but a clear פסוק names the instrument. 'בכסה' is read as 'covered', pointing to the day the new moon cannot be seen. That locks in שופר and blocks trumpets.

keyTerms.meaning: at the covered time (when the moon is hidden)
the Merciful One (ה׳, in His Torah)

steps.whatToRemember: The blowing pattern can come from the wilderness, but the instrument on ראש השנה is a שופר, because the פסוק in תהלים says so.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'Blow a shofar at the new month,
at the covered time, for our festival day,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:4. The גמרא reads בכסה as 'covered', like the moon hiding.

phrases.english: Which is the festival
on which the moon is covered?
You must say this is Rosh Hashanah,
and the Merciful One says: 'shofar'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֵּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the trumpet challenge in Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit פסוק limits how far the comparison reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe ראש השנה needs trumpets, just like the wilderness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק about the festival of the covered moon names שופר, so only a שופר is used.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's order of blasts in קיסרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו set up in קיסרי an order of תקיעה, three שברים, תרועה, תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו set up in קיסרי: a תקיעה, three שברים, a תרועה, and a תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: the גמרא reports the order of blasts that רבי אבהו instituted in his city, קיסרי. This sets up a challenge that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the plain blasts surrounded one middle sound. רבי אבהו put two kinds of broken sounds in the middle: שברים and then תרועה. The question will be why both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: instituted, set up as a practice
קיסרי, a city in ארץ ישראל
broken sounds, a few medium blasts

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu instituted in Caesarea:
a tekiah, three shevarim,
a teruah, a tekiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about the order of the blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קיסרי, the order is תקיעה, three שברים, תרועה, תקיעה.

steps.title: Why blow both שברים and תרועה?
steps.stepSummary: Whatever the Torah's תרועה is, רבי אבהו should blow only one kind of sound between the plain blasts, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if the תרועה is a wailing sound, he should do תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. And if it is a groaning sound, he should do תקיעה, three שברים, תקיעה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's order. The Torah's תרועה is either one kind of sound or the other, so why put both in one set?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand the Torah's תרועה: short wailing sounds (our תרועה) or longer groaning sounds (our שברים). Each view needs only its own sound in the middle. Putting both together seems to add a sound that, on either view, does not belong there.

keyTerms.meaning: whichever way you look at it

steps.confusionAlert: This is a challenge, not the final practice. The גמרא is asking why both sounds appear in one set, and the answer comes next.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if the teruah is a wailing,
let him do tekiah, teruah, and tekiah;
and if it is a groaning,
let him do tekiah, three shevarim, and tekiah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order רבי אבהו set up in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's order of תקיעה, שברים, תרועה, תקיעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On either reading of the Torah's תרועה, only one of the two middle sounds is right, so blowing both in one set makes no sense.

steps.title: רבי אבהו was unsure which sound the Torah means
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו put both שברים and תרועה in the middle because he was unsure whether the Torah's תרועה is moaning or whimpering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was in doubt whether the Torah's תרועה is moaning or whimpering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 34: רבי אבהו blew both kinds of sound because he did not know which one the Torah means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moaning means longer broken sighs, which is the שברים sound. Whimpering means short quick sobs, which is the תרועה sound. Since רבי אבהו could not decide, he included both so that one of them would surely be right.

keyTerms.meaning: He was in doubt; he was unsure
Whimpering or wailing, short quick sobs (like תְּרוּעָה)

phrases.english: He was in doubt
whether [the תרועה] is moaning
phrases.notes: Moaning matches the שברים sound, three medium sighs. Whimpering matches the תרועה sound, short rapid blasts.

phrases.english: or whimpering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אִי גַּנּוֹחֵי גַּנַּח אִי יַלּוֹלֵי יַלֵּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 34 about why both sounds are blown.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבהו should blow only one type of sound, whichever the Torah means.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the meaning is uncertain, he blew both to be sure.

steps.title: Rav Avira: the extra שברים might break the set
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא objects that if the true sound is whimpering, the added שברים come between the first תקיעה and the תרועה and spoil the set.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא objected: But maybe the תרועה is whimpering, and then the three שברים interrupt between the תרועה and the first תקיעה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא challenges רבי אבהו's combined set: blowing an extra sound might not just be useless, it might actually ruin the set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper set must be a plain blast, then the middle sound, then a plain blast, with nothing in between. If the real sound is the תרועה, the שברים are a stranger stuck between the first תקיעה and the תרועה. That interruption could make the whole set invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that the extra sound is wasted. The worry is that it interrupts, which could make the whole set count for nothing.

phrases.english: Rav Avira objected to this:
But perhaps it is whimpering,
and the three שברים interrupt
between the תרועה and the תקיעה!
phrases.notes: He means the first תקיעה, the one blown before the שברים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עַוִּירָא וְדִלְמָא יַלּוֹלֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 35 by showing that adding both sounds may harm the set.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the true sound is the תרועה, the שברים form an interruption that disqualifies the set.

steps.title: That is why he also blows תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי אבהו also has a separate תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה set, which covers the whimpering possibility cleanly.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why he then does a תקיעה, תרועה, and תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even if the combined set fails, the separate simple set with only the תרועה covers the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו did not rely only on the combined set. He also set up a clean set with just the תרועה in the middle. So if the true sound is whimpering, that set does the job without any interruption.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why he goes back and does

phrases.english: That is why he goes back and does
a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עוירא's objection in step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תרועה is whimpering, the combined set is ruined and nothing works.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה set covers that possibility.

steps.title: רבינא: the extra תרועה might break the set
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects from the other side: if the true sound is moaning, the תרועה comes between the שברים and the last תקיעה and spoils the set.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: But maybe it is moaning, and then the תרועה interrupts between the שברים and the final תקיעה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises the same kind of problem, but for the opposite possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the real sound is the שברים, then the תרועה blown after them is an extra sound. It sits between the שברים and the last תקיעה, so it could invalidate the combined set.

phrases.english: Ravina objected to this:
But perhaps it is moaning,
and the תרועה interrupts
between the שברים and the תקיעה!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא וְדִלְמָא גַּנּוֹחֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רב עוירא's objection in step 36, but for the moaning possibility.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the true sound is the שברים, the תרועה is an interruption before the final תקיעה.

steps.title: That is why he also blows תקיעה-שברים-תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a separate תקיעה-שברים-תקיעה set covers the moaning possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why he then does a תקיעה, שברים, תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer: a clean set with only the שברים covers this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now all three sets have shown up. One set is combined, one has only שברים, and one has only תרועה. Each simple set protects against the interruption problem raised for its possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: Three medium broken blasts, sounding like moaning

phrases.english: That is why he goes back and does
a תקיעה, שברים, and a תקיעה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's objection in step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תרועה is moaning, the combined set is ruined.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate תקיעה-שברים-תקיעה set covers that possibility.

steps.title: Then why is the combined set needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the two simple sets already cover moaning and whimpering, what did רבי אבהו add with the combined set?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what did רבי אבהו institute? If it is moaning, he already did it. If it is whimpering, he already did it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answers around: if the simple sets cover everything, the combined set seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 37 and 39 showed that each possibility has its own clean set. That makes רבי אבהו's special combined set look unnecessary, since both options are already handled.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he institute? (What did his rule add?)

phrases.english: But then what did רבי אבהו institute?
If it is moaning,
he already did it;
if it is whimpering,
he already did it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answers of steps 37 and 39 to question the need for רבי אבהו's combined set.
steps.kashyaTarget: The purpose of רבי אבהו's combined set
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possibilities are already covered by the simple sets, so the combined set adds nothing.

steps.title: Maybe the sound is moaning and then whimpering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו also considered a third possibility: the Torah's תרועה is moaning followed by whimpering, which only the combined set covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was in doubt: perhaps it is moaning and then whimpering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that there is a third option, both sounds together, and the combined set is the one that covers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's doubt had three sides, not two. The תרועה might be only moaning, only whimpering, or moaning followed by whimpering. So all three sets are needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו's three sets match three possibilities: שברים alone, תרועה alone, or שברים followed by תרועה.

phrases.english: He was in doubt:
perhaps it is moaning and whimpering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 40 by adding a third possibility.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only two options exist, so the combined set is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: A third option, moaning followed by whimpering, requires the combined set.

steps.title: Then also blow the reverse order
steps.stepSummary: If the sound might be moaning then whimpering, maybe it is whimpering then moaning, so a תקיעה-תרועה-שברים-תקיעה set should be added.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him also do the reverse: תקיעה, תרועה, three שברים, and תקיעה, since perhaps it is whimpering and then moaning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the logic further: if combinations count, the opposite order should be covered too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we allow a mixed sound, there seems to be no reason to pick only one order. So the גמרא asks why there is no fourth set with the תרועה first.

phrases.english: If so,
let him also do the reverse:
תקיעה, תרועה, three שברים, and תקיעה,
since perhaps it is whimpering and then moaning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of step 41 to demand a reverse-order set.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the combined set to one order
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a mixed sound is possible, the opposite mixture is equally possible.

steps.title: People first moan and then whimper
steps.stepSummary: Normally a person in trouble first moans and only then breaks into whimpering, so the reverse order is not a real possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: The normal way of things is that when something bad happens to a person, first he moans and then he whimpers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from how people really cry: the natural order is moaning first, then whimpering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרועה is modeled on the sound of a person crying. Real crying starts with long sighs and turns into short sobs, never the other way around. So only the order שברים then תרועה needs to be covered.
steps.whatToRemember: The combined set goes שברים then תרועה because that is how a person naturally cries.

phrases.english: The normal way of things is
when something bad happens to a person,
first he moans
and then he whimpers.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְתָמָא דְמִילְּתָא כִּי מִתְּרַע בְּאִינִישׁ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 42 and closes the discussion of רבי אבהו's sets.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either order of mixed sounds is possible, so both should be blown.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only moaning-then-whimpering is natural, so no reverse set is needed.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: stretching the second blast as two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about someone who blew the first תקיעה and stretched the second to count for two. Then רבי יוחנן begins a comment on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If he blew the first, and stretched the second as long as two. רבי יוחנן said: If one heard...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה, and opens רבי יוחנן's comment on it. His statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who tries to make one long blast count as the end of one set and the start of the next. The משנה counts it as only one blast. This step sets up the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: And he stretched out (made it longer)

phrases.english: If he blew the first [תקיעה]
and stretched the second as long as two,
רבי יוחנן said: If one heard

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי אבהו's sets and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case of stretching the second תקיעה to count as two; רבי יוחנן's comment on it begins here.
